title: Concurrency pacing regression - scrapbook
content:
Notes: this is my scratchpad while ruling out pacing/synchronization causes for the late-Feb throughput regression. Goal: be able to repro with a synthetic harness and validate whether the token-bucket/worker-lease interaction is causing batch formation to stall intermittently. Do not treat as finished.

Summary:
- Symptom: overall tokens/sec dropped ~18% during 2025-02-15 evening deploy; tail latency increased for 95/99p while p50 roughly same. No obvious capacity shortage (GPU utilization steady).
- Hypothesis (primary): pacing controller (per-device rate limiter) and batch-aggregator are occasionally entering a synchronized slow-mode due to lease-renewal + rate-token refill misalignment -> short windows where batches are not emitted and requests queue up, then large batches hit the runtime causing microbursts and throttling.
- Alternative hypotheses: autoscaler backoff oscillation, host-level cgroup interference, networking TC shaping in new k8s nodepool.

Timeline / quick hits:
- 2025-02-15 18:12 UTC: deploy 2025.02.15.1 (small change to batching heuristic: prefer-early-emit when queue_size > N).
- 2025-02-15 20:03 UTC: first customer reports higher latency. Internal alert (throughput drop) fired at 20:10.
- 2025-02-15 20:45 UTC: rolled back to previous config on a canary subset; canary latencies returned to baseline.
- 2025-02-16 03:30 UTC: full rollback applied. Regression not fully reverted for some routes -> suggests config/stateful per-host condition.

Observability queries I ran (PromQL / ClickHouse):
- prom: rate(inference_tokens_total{model=~".*-4.*"}[5m]) by (instance) -> showed per-host drop clusters.
- prom: sum(rate(incoming_requests[1m])) by (zone) vs sum(rate(rejections[1m])) -> rejections (quota) not increasing.
- CH: SELECT quantiles(0.5,0.95,0.99)(lat_ms) FROM request_metrics WHERE route = 'chat' AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY GROUP BY host
- result: hosts with lower tokens/sec had high p99 and long flat tails on request wait_time_ms metric (queue_time).

Reproduction steps attempted (local harness):
1) baseline load generator (runtimes/test-harness):
   - python tools/loadgen.py --qps 120 --payload-size 512 --concurrency 200 --duration 10m
   - Observed: normal batching, stable throughput.
2) add jitter to arrival pattern to simulate burstiness:
   - python tools/loadgen.py --qps 120 --jitter 0.6 --concurrency 200
   - Observed: transient larger batches, slight p99 increase but throughput ok.
3) emulate lease-renewal lag / slow heartbeat by pausing agent thread (local patch):
   - patched aggregator to sleep (0.15s) when lease_renewal returns false (dev-only).
   - Observed: queues built up for ~300ms then flushed as large batch; throughput drop and higher tail latencies similar to incident. This seems promising.

Commands / logs captured during an incident-host run (sanitized):
- tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/agg.log | grep "emit_batch"
  [2025-02-15T20:07:58Z] host=a1 emit_batch size=12 wall_ms=43
  [2025-02-15T20:08:11Z] host=a1 emit_batch size=71 wall_ms=512  # big flush
  [2025-02-15T20:08:12Z] host=a1 emit_batch size=4 wall_ms=37
  [2025-02-15T20:08:20Z] host=a1 emit_batch size=66 wall_ms=488  # repeating pattern
- grep "pacer" /var/log/redwood/pacer.log
  [2025-02-15T20:07:58Z] pacer: refill_tokens +120 (now 240)
  [2025-02-15T20:08:10Z] pacer: token_bucket empty -> stall
  [2025-02-15T20:08:11Z] pacer: refill_tokens +500 (burst policy) -> emit
  [2025-02-15T20:08:12Z] pacer: tokens left 10
  [2025-02-15T20:08:19Z] pacer: token_bucket empty -> stall

Error snippets / stack traces seen (truncated):
- WARN aggregator "emit delay exceeded threshold" lease_renewal_ms=210 available_tokens=0
- ERROR workerpool "dispatch timeout" worker_id=17 pending_batches=2
- DEBUG net "write: connection reset by peer"  (customer retries)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token-bucket refill and lease-renewal operate on separate clocks; under certain traffic patterns the refill schedule lines up such that several devices enter an empty-window simultaneously. Combined with prefer-early-emit change, the aggregator waits for tokens -> produces large batches infrequently -> throughput drop.
2) New k8s nodepool uses different CPU scheduling (burstable classes) causing small pauses in the pacer thread, making refill jitter larger than expected.
3) Rate-limit config change (we widened burst allowance) created rare large refills that destabilize rolling average used by autoscaler -> autoscaler throttle visibility causes host-level pacing adjustments.
4) GC/Stop-the-world pause in python-based helper process (observed 60-80ms occasionally) correlates with big flush events.

Quick experiments to validate/falsify:
- Force pacer refill to be monotonic jitter-free in dev harness (patch pacer to use monotonic timer). If repro goes away -> clocking/jitter root cause.
- Disable prefer-early-emit flag on canaries and measure; A/B showed canary rollback improved in prod earlier -> confirm with controlled test.
- Add per-host random jitter (10-30ms) to refill offset to break alignment. If throughput baseline returns, indicates synchronization resonance.

Temporary mitigations (low-risk):
- Add small random jitter to token refill on all hosts (config flag pacing.refill_jitter_ms=20).
- Reduce max-burst-refill magnitude (pacing.max_refill_burst=150 -> 100) to avoid huge sudden refills.
- Roll back prefer-early-emit change on affected release branches (already done on canary).

Instrumentation / follow-ups to add:
- Histogram of inter-emit intervals per-host (new metric: batch_emit_interval_ms) and alert when > 200ms with count>5 in a minute.
- Trace full path from request enqueue -> batch emit -> worker dispatch, sample 1% of requests when emit_size > 50 for detailed stack traces.
- Export pacer internal state (tokens, last_refill_ts, refill_delta_ms) to tracing span for correlation.

Next steps (TODO):
- [ ] Push dev patch that adds deterministic refill jitter and run cluster-level soak for 6 hours (Ravi).
- [ ] Add unit/integration test that simulates lease-renewal fail and asserts no > 250ms stall (measured in harness) (Maya).
- [ ] Instrument batch_emit_interval_ms and create a short-lived dashboard; hook anomaly alerts (Zoe).
- [ ] Prepare RCA note if experiment confirms pacing sync as root cause and propose permanent fix (decrease burst + jitter).

Notes-to-self: avoid overfitting to single-host log samples. Need cluster-wide aggregates. Also check whether any recent kernel updates or k8s nodepool images changed NTP/clocksource (we saw related issues before).

Observational artefact: when large flush occurs we see many small retry attempts from clients (backoff) which can feed the next big flush -> feedback loop. Consider smoothing client backoff jitter to avoid feeding resonance in server-side batching.
